parsed_response.reasoning: The diff confirms the mechanism: GoogleCalendarService's createEvent was changed to accept `credentialId` and select the matching destination calendar (`calEventRaw.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.credentialId === credentialId)?.externalId`), while EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents now loops over all destinations calling `createEvent(credential, event, destination.externalId)`. However, the Lark/Office365 services were only mechanically migrated to the array type (`const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = event.destinationCalendar ?? []` in larkcalendar) and their createEvent signatures were not extended to receive the credentialId/destination, so each per-host createEvent call ignores which destination it was invoked for and uses only the first host's calendar. This means multi-host (collective) bookings with non-Google destination calendars are written to the wrong/first calendar rather than each host's calendar — a concrete correctness gap introduced by this diff.

judged_text: Only GoogleCalendarService was updated to select the destination calendar matching the passed credentialId; larkcalendar (and office365calendar) still destructure only the first destination calendar (`const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = event.destinationCalendar ?? []`), so the multi-host feature silently no-ops for non-Google hosts. A collective event whose non-organizer hosts use Lark or Office 365 calendars gets written only to the first host's calendar even though the destinationCalendar array carries all hosts' entries — team members' calendars never receive the event and no error or warning is raised, leaving users with a partial multi-host implementation that differs by integration.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `CalendarEvent.destinationCalendar` to an array and `EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents` now iterates over all destinations, calling `createEvent(credential, event, destination.externalId)` for each host destination. However, non-Google calendar services still select only the first destination calendar: e.g. `packages/app-store/larkcalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts` uses `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = event.destinationCalendar ?? []; const calendarId = mainHostDestinationCalendar?.externalId;`, and `packages/app-store/office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts` similarly builds the URL from the first entry. In contrast, GoogleCalendarService was updated to pick the destination matching the passed `credentialId`. This means for multi-host collective events with mixed integrations, Lark/Office365 will repeatedly write to the first destination calendar regardless of which credential is being processed, so team members’ calendars won’t receive events even though the array contains them.
